newsitem.title: USA: Texas border patrol unhappy with loss of agents.
newsitem.headline: Texas border patrol unhappy with loss of agents.

text.p: Border Patrol officials in Texas said on Friday that a fresh push to fight illegal immigration in California could hurt immigration and anti-drug efforts elsewhere.

Doris Meissner, commissioner of the Immigration and Naturalisation Service, said on Thursday that 200 agents, a horse patrol and underground sensors would be sent from next week to boost border patrols in California.
But agents in Texas said on Friday the reinforcements for California were simply being transferred from other areas.

"They're cracking down on illegal immigration in California and Arizona and that's causing our problem here to swell. We need more agents, not less," said William Veal, head of the El Paso Sector Border Patrol.
He said he would lose 18 agents to California. Veal currently has 480 agents, including 70 additional agents assigned to the sector this year, but said he needs at least 150 more.
Illegal immigration has climbed 31 percent in this area so far this year and narcotics seizures are up 23 percent.
Veal's assistant, Jaime Arras, said the redeployment of 18 agents from Texas to California "couldn't come at a worse time and we're not happy about it, but there's nothing we can do."
